note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: You are setting out the electrical positions for a new two-storey house in Mandeville. Which documents should you have before you start?
options: Only the customer's spoken instructions from the first visit
The current-revision drawings, specification and schedules
The electricity bill from the house the customer lives in now
A photo of a similar house that another firm has wired

questions.stem: A datum line is marked 1 000 mm above FFL (finished floor level). A switch box must be centred 1 200 mm above FFL. Where is its centre marked?
options: 1 200 mm above the datum
200 mm below the datum
2 200 mm above FFL
200 mm above the datum

questions.stem: Why is the height written beside a datum line on the wall, for example "datum 1 000 mm above FFL"?
options: So every trade reads heights from the same known line
So the painter knows which colour to use on the wall
So the line can be wiped off once the boxes are fixed
So the customer can check the price of the work

questions.stem: A datum line is to be marked around all four walls of a room. Which tool does this fastest and most accurately?
options: A short spirit level moved along the wall a bit at a time
A tape measure from the rough floor at every metre
A self-levelling line laser, checked for accuracy first
A chalk line held loosely at each end by two workers

questions.stem: How can you check that a line laser is still giving a true level line?
options: Look at the line; if it is bright and sharp, it is level
Compare it with the top edge of a door frame or window in the room
Mark the line on two walls, turn the laser round, and compare
Switch it off and on again to reset its levelling

questions.stem: A marked fixing point is directly above an existing socket outlet. What should you suspect before drilling?
options: A cable may run straight up from the outlet through that spot
Nothing, because cables never run straight above an outlet
The wall will be hollow at that point, so the fixing will be stronger
The outlet will need to be moved up to the new fixing point

questions.stem: A cable detector shows nothing behind a marked spot on a block wall. How should you treat this result?
options: The wall is certainly clear, so drill at full speed
The detector must be broken if it found nothing
Drill a larger hole to make sure nothing is missed
Treat it as a guide only and still check the drawings

questions.stem: On a 1:50 drawing, a socket outlet is 64 mm from a wall corner. How far is it from the corner on site?
options: 640 mm

questions.stem: The drawing shows a box at 1 200 mm above FFL, but the specification says 1 100 mm. What should you do?
options: Ask the supervisor or designer which one is right
Use the drawing, since drawings are always right
Split the difference and fix it at 1 150 mm
Use whichever height is quicker to reach

questions.stem: A cable trench must leave a building wall at 90°. You measure 1.2 m along the wall and 1.6 m out along the trench line. What should the diagonal between the two marks be if the angle is square?
Why is a conduit drop marked with a plumb line or laser, rather than measured parallel to the nearest door frame?
options: Door frames are always fitted at 45° to the wall
The frame may not be truly vertical, so the drop would lean
A plumb line is quicker to read than any tape measure
Conduit must always run at an angle to door frames

questions.stem: You must cut a rectangular hole in a steel enclosure door for a panel meter. What is the best first step?
options: Drill a hole in the middle and cut outward until it fits
Hold the meter against the door and draw round it by eye
Cut the hole with a grinder, then mark the fixing holes
Mark the centre lines from a datum edge, then the outline

questions.stem: Before marking cut-outs on an enclosure door, why should you check the positions with the door closed?
options: To make the marking lines easier to see in daylight
To stop the door's hinges from wearing out
So that the paint on the door is not scratched
So that devices on the door clear parts inside the box

questions.stem: The corners of a rectangular cut-out are drilled before it is cut with a nibbler or jigsaw. Where are the corner holes marked?
options: Outside the outline, so the hole ends up larger
Just inside the outline, touching the corner lines
At the centre of each side, not at the corners
Anywhere inside the outline, as long as they fit

questions.stem: Several cable glands must fit side by side in a gland plate. What decides the spacing between hole centres?
options: The width of the electrician's hand, to reach in behind
The size of the drill bit and nothing else
Room for each gland's locknut and a spanner to turn it
The number of cores inside the largest cable on the plate

questions.stem: Why is a gland plate usually removed from the enclosure before its holes are marked and cut?
options: So swarf does not fall onto the parts inside the enclosure
So the plate can be painted before it is fitted again
So the holes can be cut a little larger than the drawing shows
So the enclosure is lighter to lift during the job

questions.stem: You will use a knockout punch to make a 25 mm hole in a steel enclosure. What do you mark and drill first?
options: The full 25 mm hole, which the punch then makes cleaner
The centre, then a pilot hole for the punch's draw bolt
A square outline round the hole, then cut it with a hacksaw
Nothing, because the punch finds its own centre

questions.stem: When marking out the layout of a control panel back plate, why is space left between rows of devices for trunking?
options: So wires can be routed neatly and devices can be changed
So the panel weighs less when it is hung on the wall
So the back plate can bend without the devices touching
So the devices can be fitted without using any screws

questions.stem: A drive's maker says to leave 100 mm clear above and below it. Why must this space be marked out before other devices are placed?
options: So the drive's label can be read from the floor
So the drive can be fitted upside down later
So air can flow through it and it does not overheat
So the panel door can be locked from the inside

questions.stem: A 2.4 m length of trunking needs fixings no more than 600 mm apart, with one fixing 100 mm from each end. What is the fewest number of fixings?
Five fixings are spaced equally along a 2.4 m length of trunking, with the end ones 100 mm from each end. What is the spacing between fixings?
options: 550 mm
480 mm
600 mm
440 mm

questions.stem: A chalk line is snapped along a 7 m wall, but the line comes out curved. What is the most likely cause?
options: The chalk was the wrong colour for the wall
The wall was painted too recently for the chalk to hold on it
The line was too short for the length of the wall
The line was not pulled tight or was snapped at an angle

questions.stem: Four ceiling lights are to be equally spaced along a 10 m room, with half a space between each end wall and the nearest light. What is the distance between lights?
Two DIN rails, 150 mm apart, are to be centred top to bottom on a back plate 500 mm high. How far below the top edge is the upper rail?
options: 150 mm
250 mm
175 mm
325 mm

questions.stem: Lights are set out on a ceiling as a grid. Which is the best way to make sure the grid is square to the room?
options: Measure every light from the nearest wall only
Start from one corner and step along by eye
Set out two centre lines at 90° and measure from them
Follow the joints of the ceiling boards wherever they go

questions.stem: The specification says boxes in a row must be level within ±3 mm. One box is marked 5 mm higher than the datum height. What should happen?
options: Leave it, since 5 mm cannot be seen by most people
Mark it as out of tolerance and reset it before fixing
Move all the other boxes up 5 mm so they match it
Fill the gap with plaster later to hide the step

questions.stem: A bracket's fixing holes must line up with holes already drilled in a steel frame. What is the most accurate way to mark them?
options: Hold the bracket in place and mark through its holes
Measure each hole from the floor with a tape
Estimate the positions from a photo of the frame
Drill new holes in the frame to suit any bracket

questions.stem: The rough floor along a 10 m wall slopes by 30 mm from one end to the other. Where should box heights be measured from?
options: The rough floor directly under each box
The ceiling, which is always more level than the floor
The top of the skirting board along the wall
A level datum line marked along the whole wall

questions.stem: You set out the position of a meter post outdoors. Why are offset pegs placed outside the digging area, rather than one peg on the exact spot?
options: Pegs are cheaper than marking paint
String lines help keep the soil from falling in
So the customer can see where the work is from the road
So the position can be found again after digging

questions.stem: A cable trench must keep a set distance from a water pipe shown on the site plan. What should be done before marking the trench line?
options: Find and mark the pipe's real position on site
Trust the site plan and mark from the boundary
Dig a test hole anywhere along the planned line
Ask the digger driver to keep well clear of pipes

questions.stem: Which is the best way to mark hole positions on a painted steel enclosure that will stay on show?
options: A scriber, cutting deep into the paint
A heavy centre punch on every mark
Masking tape with pencil marks on the tape
Spray paint through a card stencil

questions.stem: Why is a centre punch used only lightly on thin sheet-metal enclosures?
options: Thin sheet is too hard for a punch to mark
A heavy blow can dent or distort the panel
The punch mark will rust away within a day
Thin sheet needs no mark before drilling

questions.stem: After a small pilot hole is drilled, which tool makes a clean round hole for a 22 mm pilot light in a thin steel enclosure door?
options: A flat wood spade bit
A step drill or punch
A masonry drill bit
A countersink bit

questions.stem: Who should check a large panel's marked cut-outs and drill positions before any cutting starts?
options: Nobody; cutting quickly saves the most time
The customer, who will use the panel later
A second competent person, against the drawing
The delivery driver who brought the enclosure

questions.stem: During set-out you find that a wall has been built 300 mm away from where the drawing shows it. What should you do?
options: Mark everything as drawn and ignore the wall
Ask the builder to move the wall to where it is drawn
Choose new box positions without telling anyone
Stop, record it, and ask the supervisor for direction

questions.stem: You need to mark ceiling light positions 3.5 m above the floor. Which method avoids most of the work at height?
options: Mark them on the floor, then transfer up with a plumb laser
Measure each light along the ceiling with a tape, from a ladder
Stand on chairs and measure along the ceiling
Guess the positions and correct them after fixing

questions.stem: Marked fixing holes are being drilled into a concrete ceiling. Which PPE matters most?
options: Eye protection and a dust mask
Welding gloves and a leather apron
A hairnet and disposable shoe covers
Rubber boots and a life jacket

questions.stem: Why is a conduit route marked on the wall before any saddles are fixed?
options: So the conduit can be bought after the job is done
So the electrician does not need to measure any of the bends
So the saddles can be fixed at any spacing at all
To check it is straight, clear and as short as practical

questions.stem: Forty houses on a housing scheme have the same kitchen layout. How can box positions be marked quickly and the same each time?
options: Measure each kitchen from scratch with new figures
Make a checked template or rod with the positions on it
Ask each installer to choose the positions they prefer
Mark only the first kitchen and copy the rest by eye

questions.stem: How can a water level (a clear tube filled with water) help when setting out?
options: It shows the exact depth to dig a cable trench along a wall
It shows whether a wall or a conduit drop is truly vertical
It carries a level height round corners and between rooms
It measures the straight distance between two boxes

questions.stem: A box must finish flush with the plaster, and the wall will get 15 mm of plaster. How should the box be set when it is marked and fixed?
options: Flush with the bare blockwork
Sunk 15 mm deeper than the blockwork
Standing 15 mm out from the blockwork
Standing 30 mm out from the blockwork

questions.stem: A 400 mm DIN rail must be centred across a 450 mm wide back plate. How far in from each edge does the rail start?
options: 25 mm
50 mm
225 mm
200 mm

questions.stem: A cable tray turns 30° on a flat roof. On a 1 m baseline, how far out from the baseline is the 30° line at the 1 m mark? (tan 30° ≈ 0.577)
options: 500 mm
866 mm
577 mm

questions.stem: Your team is marking out boxes in six rooms at once. How do you make sure everyone works to the same heights?
options: Let each person choose a height that looks right
Give everyone the same datum and a checked height list
Have each person copy the room next to theirs
Use the height of each room's door handle

questions.stem: After the set-out is checked, why should any changes agreed on site be marked on the drawing?
options: So the drawing looks busier for the customer
So the original drawing can be thrown away
So the as-built record shows what was really done
So the supervisor does not need to visit the site

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences and show any working. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name for a level reference line marked around a room, from which all heights are measured?
A 1:20 drawing shows a distance of 45 mm. What is the real distance, in millimetres?
What is the name of the tool that snaps a straight coloured line onto a wall or floor?
A trench is set out at 90° to a wall with the 3-4-5 method, using 0.9 m along the wall as the '3'. How far along the trench line, in metres, is the '4' mark?
What do we call the strips of wall, in line with an outlet or switch, where hidden cables are expected to run?
What is the name of the tool, used with a pilot hole and a draw bolt, that cuts clean round holes in steel enclosures?
Five downlights are equally spaced in a 7.5 m corridor, with half a space at each end. What is the spacing between downlights, in metres?
What is the name of the long, straight strip marked with heights, used to transfer the same box heights to many walls?
What is the name of the drawing that shows how an installation was really built, including the changes made on site?
Which hand-held tool cuts a rectangular hole in sheet steel by taking small bites along the marked line?
What is the name of the threaded bolt that pulls a knockout punch through the metal?
A 35 mm deep box must stand 15 mm proud of the blockwork to allow for plaster. How deep, in millimetres, must the recess in the block be?
A height is given as 1 200 mm ± 2 mm. What is the lowest acceptable height, in millimetres?
What is the name of the removable steel plate, at the top or bottom of an enclosure, that is drilled for the cable glands?
Write, as a ratio, the scale of a drawing on which 1 mm stands for 100 mm on site.

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and set out the positions of all the switches, socket outlets, lights and the distribution board in one room of a new house, from the drawings to the final check.
essays.modelAnswer: I first make sure I have the latest revision of the drawings, the specification and the schedules, and I read the heights and any notes. I walk the room and compare it with the drawing, noting any differences such as doors or windows in different places. I mark a level datum line round the room with a checked line laser, and measure all heights from it, not from the rough floor. I find the room's key reference points, such as wall corners and door openings, and measure positions along the walls from them. I check for hidden services with a detector and the drawings. I mark each box outline and centre clearly, label what it is, and mark ceiling light positions by setting them out on the floor and transferring them up with a plumb laser. Finally a second person checks every position against the drawing, and any agreed change is written on the drawing.
markingPoints: Uses current drawings, specification and schedules
Compares the room with the drawing and notes differences
Marks a level datum and measures heights from it
Checks for hidden services and marks and labels clearly
Checks against the drawing by a second person and records changes

essays.stem: Explain how you would set up a datum line through several rooms of a building, and how you would check that the equipment used is accurate.
essays.modelAnswer: I start from a reference height given by the builder, usually a mark showing a set height above finished floor level. I set a self-levelling line laser in the first room and mark the datum line on every wall, at the same height above the reference. To carry the height into the next room, I mark a point near the doorway and set the laser up again in the new room, matching that point; a water level can also carry a height round corners. Before use, I check the laser: I mark its line on two facing walls, turn it round 180°, mark again, and compare. If the marks differ by more than the maker allows, the laser is sent for adjustment. I also check the line against the builder's reference at the far end of the building. I write the datum height on the walls, for example "datum 1 000 mm above FFL", so every trade uses the same line.
markingPoints: Starts from the builder's reference height above FFL
Uses a line laser or water level to mark all walls
Carries the height between rooms from a common point
Checks the laser by turning it round between two walls
Labels the datum height and checks at the far end

essays.stem: Describe how you would mark out and cut a steel enclosure door for one panel meter, two push buttons and a pilot light, so that the finished door looks neat and the devices fit.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the drawing and each device maker's cut-out sizes, and check them against the real devices. With the door closed, I check that nothing on the door will hit parts inside. I take the door off and lay it flat on a clean, padded bench. I put masking tape where the holes will go so the paint is not scratched. I mark a vertical and a horizontal centre line from a datum edge, then mark each device's centre, and the meter's rectangle from its centre lines. A second person checks the marking against the drawing. For the round holes I lightly punch the centres, drill small pilot holes, and open them to size with a step drill or knockout punch. For the rectangle I drill a hole just inside each corner and cut along the lines with a nibbler or jigsaw. I file and deburr every edge, remove the tape, clean off swarf, and test-fit each device.
markingPoints: Uses the drawing and makers' cut-out sizes and checks clearance inside
Removes the door, protects the paint, marks centre lines from a datum
Has the marking checked before cutting
Uses pilot holes, step drill or punch, and corner holes for the rectangle
Deburrs, cleans swarf and test-fits devices

essays.stem: Explain how you would lay out and mark the back plate of a small control panel with a main isolator, DIN-rail devices, a drive and terminal rails.
essays.modelAnswer: I start from the panel drawing and the makers' data for each item: sizes, fixing holes and the clear space each needs. I put the main isolator where the incoming cable arrives, usually near the top or the gland plate, so the incoming supply cable is short. The drive goes where it has the clear space above and below that its maker asks for, so air can flow, and away from heat-sensitive items. DIN rails are marked level from a datum edge, with trunking between each row so wires run neatly and devices can be changed. Terminal rails go near the gland plate so outgoing cables are easy to connect. I leave some spare space for later additions. I mark rail and trunking positions with a square and rule from the datum, have a second person check the layout against the drawing, and only then drill and fix.
markingPoints: Works from the drawing and makers' sizes and clearances
Isolator placed near the incoming supply
Drive placed with its ventilation clearances
Rails level from a datum with trunking between rows, terminals near the glands
Leaves spare space and checks before drilling

essays.stem: Six lights are to be set out in a 9 m × 6 m room as a grid of 3 rows of 2 lights, with half a space between each wall and the nearest light. Work out the positions and describe how you would mark them accurately on the ceiling.
essays.modelAnswer: Along the 9 m length there are 3 lights, so the spacing is 9 ÷ 3 = 3 m, and the first light is 1.5 m from each end wall. Across the 6 m width there are 2 lights, so the spacing is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 m, and each light is 1.5 m from the side walls. So the lights are at 1.5 m, 4.5 m and 7.5 m along the room, and 1.5 m and 4.5 m across it. I mark the room's two centre lines on the floor, checking that they cross at 90° with the 3-4-5 method or by checking that the diagonals of the grid are equal. I mark each light position on the floor from the centre lines, then transfer each one to the ceiling with a plumb laser, so most of the work is done from the floor. I check the spacing on the ceiling and compare it with the drawing before any holes are made.
markingPoints: 3 m spacing along with 1.5 m at the ends
3 m spacing across with 1.5 m at the sides
Positions listed correctly
Centre lines set out square (3-4-5 or equal diagonals)
Transfers marks up with a plumb laser and checks before drilling

essays.stem: Describe how you would set out the route of an underground cable trench from a building to a gate light 25 m away, including the safety checks before any digging.
essays.modelAnswer: I study the site plan and any drawings of existing services, such as water, sewer, telephone and power cables, and ask the owner what they know. I use a cable and pipe detector along the planned route and mark any services found with paint or pegs. I then mark the route: a peg at the building, a peg at the gate light position, and a string line between them, checking the distance and keeping the required distance from other services. Where the trench leaves the building I check it is square to the wall with the 3-4-5 method. I put offset pegs to the side of the route, so the line can be found again after digging. I mark the trench width and depth from the specification. The route is checked by the supervisor before digging, and any hand digging near found services is planned. The route is recorded on the drawing for the as-built record.
markingPoints: Checks plans and asks about existing services
Scans the route with a detector and marks services found
Marks the line with pegs and string, checking distances
Uses offset pegs and marks width and depth
Has the route checked before digging and records it

essays.stem: Compare a spirit level, a chalk line, a line laser and a water level for setting out on site. Say what each is best for, and give one limit of each.
essays.modelAnswer: A spirit level is cheap and simple, and is good for checking that one box or a short length of trunking is level or plumb. Its limit is that over long distances small errors add up as it is moved along. A chalk line quickly marks a long straight line between two points on a wall or floor, such as a trunking route. Its limit is that it only joins the two marks: it does not find level by itself, and it can smudge or wash off. A line laser marks a level or vertical line round a whole room very quickly and accurately. Its limits are cost, the need for regular accuracy checks, and that the line is hard to see in bright sunlight. A water level carries a level height round corners and between rooms with no batteries. Its limit is that it is slow and needs care to keep air bubbles out of the tube.
markingPoints: Spirit level: short checks; errors add up over distance
Chalk line: long straight lines; does not find level, can smudge
Line laser: fast and accurate; needs checking, hard to see in sun, cost
Water level: round corners and rooms; slow, air bubbles
Clear comparison of when to use each

essays.stem: You lead a team of four setting out the electrical positions on one floor of an office block. Explain how you would organise the work and check it, so that mistakes are found before any holes are drilled.
essays.modelAnswer: Before we start, I check that everyone has the same current revision of the drawings and specification, and I explain the job, the datum and the heights to be used. I set one datum line on every wall myself, or check it, so the whole floor works from the same reference. I split the floor into areas and give each person an area, so two people do not mark the same thing differently. I give each person a checked list of heights and a marking colour or label system. During the work I walk round and spot-check positions against the drawing. When an area is finished, someone other than the person who marked it checks every position with a check sheet, and any fault is corrected. Any difference between the drawing and the building is reported to me, and I get a decision from the supervisor and mark it on the drawing. Only after sign-off does drilling start.
markingPoints: Same drawings and briefing for everyone
One datum for the whole floor
Areas shared out with a height list and labelling system
Independent check with a check sheet before drilling
Differences reported, decided and marked on the drawing

essays.stem: While setting out, you find a concrete beam exactly where the drawing shows a ceiling light. Explain what you would do and why you should not just move the light yourself.
essays.modelAnswer: I would stop marking that light and check the drawing and the site again to make sure I have not made a mistake, such as using the wrong reference wall. If the beam is really there, I would take a photo, measure where the beam is, and record it. I would report it to my supervisor and ask for a decision from the designer, giving them possible options, such as moving the light a set distance along the room or fixing it to the beam with a suitable box. I should not just move it myself, because the light's position may have been chosen for the lighting level, to line up with other lights, or to clear other services such as air-conditioning ducts. Moving it could make the room badly lit or clash with another trade. Once a decision is made, I mark the new position, note it on the drawing for the as-built record, and tell the team.
markingPoints: Rechecks own set-out against the drawing
Records the problem with measurements or photos
Reports and asks the supervisor or designer for a decision, with options
Explains why: lighting design, alignment, clashes with other trades
Marks the agreed change, records it and tells the team

essays.stem: Describe the hazards when marking out electrical work on a busy building site, and explain how you would control each one.
essays.modelAnswer: Work at height is a main hazard when marking ceilings and high walls. I control it by marking from the floor and transferring marks up with a plumb laser where possible, and otherwise using a podium or stepladder in good condition on firm ground. Hidden cables and pipes can be hit when drilling marked holes, so I check drawings, use a detector and treat existing circuits as live until isolated and proved dead. Dust from drilling concrete is controlled with eye protection, a dust mask and a vacuum. Lasers can harm the eyes, so I never look into the beam and keep it below eye level where people walk. Trip hazards from tapes, string lines and tools are controlled by keeping the area tidy and fencing outdoor pegs and lines. Other trades working nearby are a hazard too, so I agree areas with them and wear a hard hat, high-visibility vest and safety boots.
markingPoints: Work at height controlled (mark from floor, safe access)
Hidden services: drawings, detector, safe isolation
Dust and eye hazards: PPE and extraction
Laser and trip hazards controlled
Site PPE and coordination with other trades

practical1.title: Set out a training bay from a drawing: datum, boxes, trunking and ceiling lights
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a drawing of a training bay (practice walls and ceiling at the Centre) showing six boxes, a trunking route, a distribution board position and four ceiling lights, with heights given from FFL. As a group, plan the set-out and share the work: one member sets and checks the line laser and marks the datum line; each other member sets out part of the work (boxes, trunking route with fixing centres, board position, and ceiling lights marked on the floor and transferred up with a plumb laser or plumb bob). Work out the fixing centres and light spacing first and show the working. Then check another member's marks against the drawing with a check sheet, correct any errors, and mark any change on a copy of the drawing. Nothing is drilled in this task.
materials: Drawing of the training bay with heights from FFL (from the assessor)
Self-levelling line laser and plumb laser (or plumb bob)
Spirit level, chalk line, 5 m and 30 m tapes, square
Podium step or stepladder in good condition
photos: The laser accuracy check, with the two sets of marks on facing walls
The datum line marked and labelled on the walls
The box outlines and centres marked and labelled
The trunking route with fixing centres marked
The ceiling light positions marked on the floor and on the ceiling
The completed check sheet and the marked-up drawing
checklist: Took part in planning and did their share of the set-out
Worked out spacings or fixing centres correctly, with working shown
Measured heights from the datum, not from the rough floor
Marked positions accurately within the tolerance on the drawing
Labelled marks clearly so others can understand them
Checked another member's marks against the drawing and recorded the result
Used access equipment safely, or marked from the floor
Left the bay tidy, with tools and lasers put away
safety: Never look into a laser beam, and keep it out of others' eyes
Use a podium or stepladder in good condition, with a second person nearby
Keep tapes, strings and tools off the walkways
No drilling is done in this task

practical2.title: Mark out, cut and check an enclosure door and gland plate
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a steel enclosure and a drawing showing a door with a panel meter cut-out (the maker's cut-out size is given), three 22 mm holes for push buttons and a pilot light, and a gland plate with four gland holes. As a group, plan the work and the order. Each member marks out at least one feature from a datum edge, and every marking is checked by another member before cutting. Then, under the assessor's eye, members take turns to drill pilot holes, open the round holes with a step drill or knockout punch, and cut the rectangle with corner holes and a nibbler or jigsaw. Deburr every hole, clean off all swarf, and test-fit the devices and glands. Finish with an inspection sheet showing each feature's measured position against the drawing.
materials: Steel enclosure with a removable door and gland plate
Drawing with cut-out sizes (from the assessor)
Panel meter, push buttons, pilot light and glands to test-fit
Steel rule, square, vernier caliper, scriber or fine marker, masking tape, light centre punch
Drill with pilot bits, step drill or knockout punch set, nibbler or jigsaw with metal blade
Files, deburring tool, brush and vacuum for swarf
photos: The door and gland plate laid flat with masking tape, centre lines marked from the datum
The marked features with the checker's initials
A pilot hole and a hole being opened with a step drill or punch
The rectangular cut-out with its corner holes
All holes deburred and swarf cleaned away
checklist: Marked at least one feature accurately from a datum edge
Checked another member's marking against the drawing before cutting
Clamped the work securely before drilling or cutting
Used the drill, step drill or punch and the cutting tool correctly
Deburred holes and removed all swarf
Measured finished positions and recorded them on the inspection sheet
Wore eye protection and used the tools safely throughout
safety: Wear eye protection when drilling, punching and cutting; clamp the work, never hold it by hand
Do not wear gloves near a turning drill; handle sharp sheet edges with care
Check power tools and leads before use, and unplug before changing bits or blades
Clear swarf with a brush or vacuum, never with bare hands or by blowing
